description: Scan the source files, add new messages to the locale catalogs and refresh the generated types (what `verbaly extract` does). It writes the catalogs unless dryRun is set, and with the same code a second run changes nothing. prune also drops keys the code no longer references, translations included, and waits while any source file fails to parse. In a project without Verbaly, run verbaly_init first; for text still hardcoded in JSX, verbaly_wrap.

dryRun.description: Report what would change, write nothing

prune.description: Drop keys no longer referenced (deletes their translations)

root.description: Project root holding verbaly.config (defaults to the server working directory)

name: verbaly_extract

collisions.description: Keys written with more than one text: every place shows the text of the first site, so give each text its own key

escaped.description: Plural or format blocks inside a tagged template, which render as literal text

inCode.description: How many of those messages the code writes as text: 0 when the project keeps its text in the catalog and reads it with t(key)

lock.description: This run created verbaly.lock, moved an older state file (from) into it, or rewrote it whole after a merge conflict (merged): it belongs in git with the catalogs, so tell the user to commit it

messages.description: Messages the source catalog holds after this run

positional.description: Messages that hand a translator a nameless value like {_0}: put the value in a named variable first

renamed.description: Tagged templates on t under another name (const tr = useT()): never extracted, so they stay in the source language until the binding is named t

replaced.description: Source texts the code wrote over: before is what the catalog said, code is the text that ships. An edit made in the code reads like this too

stateProblem.description: The state file could not be read or written: the catalogs were written, drafts and outdated tracking were not

unparsed.description: Source files the parser could not read: their messages are not extracted, and prune drops nothing until they parse

title: Extract messages
